title: Introducing Yourself
label: ch:introductions
canDo: I can introduce myself in Sanskrit, give my name, and understand the other person's name.

payoff.summary: Complete SA-C02-practice, the canonical closing checkpoint, and demonstrate the chapter promise: introduce myself in Sanskrit, give my name, and understand the other person's name; then choose between bhavān and tvam, ask a respected stranger's name, recall the roots behind the exchange, and pick out आ, भ, ◌ि and ◌ः.
payoff.note: SA-C02-practice is the chapter's last core lesson (sequence 145), so it assesses all twenty-three atoms the chapter introduces: the exchange, the respectful and familiar 'you' with the respectful question, the roots of nāma, mama, asti, kim and ānandaḥ, and the four script shapes (reached through SA-S109-vowel-sign-i, sequence 141).
